No code change needed. If the business actually wants meghatalmazott reinstated, that's a NEW build (re-add the CHECK values, columns, RLS policies, endpoints, route guards -- everything 0044 removed), not a one-line validation fix, and should go through Istvan/business given it was an explicit Compass reversal, not route it back to me as a UAT bugfix.

**architect** · 2026-07-10 21:44

PATTERN, for future reference (this migration 0080 hit it first): any migration doing a cross-tenant backfill INSERT/UPDATE on a FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY table cannot use a plain set-based statement -- FORCE means even the table-owner/migration role is subject to the RLS policy, and a single INSERT...SELECT spanning multiple tenants has no one current_setting(app.tenant_id) value that satisfies every row at once. Correct fix: a PL/pgSQL DO block looping per-tenant, calling set_config(app.tenant_id, <id>, true) immediately before each single-tenant write -- mirrors the apps own withTenant() helper, just done manually since a migration has no ambient per-request tenant context. Example (step 1, default-site provisioning): DO $$ DECLARE r RECORD; BEGIN FOR r IN SELECT t.id, t.name FROM tenants t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM zsibongo_users u WHERE u.tenant_id=t.id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM zsibongo_sites s WHERE s.tenant_id=t.id) LOOP PERFORM set_config(app.tenant_id, r.id, true); INSERT INTO zsibongo_sites (tenant_id, name) VALUES (r.id, r.name); END LOOP; END $$; Same shape applies to steps 2/3s backfill UPDATEs on zsibongo_groups/zsibongo_users (zsibongo_groups also has FORCE RLS, migration 0024 -- will hit the identical failure if left as a plain set-based UPDATE). Safe within the migration runners single managed transaction since set_config with is_local=true resets nothing between loop iterations, just changes forward. Sent directly to Anvil (msg 10364) to iterate on the exact loop shape for steps 2/3.

**buildfejleszto** · 2026-07-10 21:46

Root cause found: zsibongo_sites AND zsibongo_groups both have FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (0021/0024), so the migration-runners pool connection (table owner) is NOT exempt on those two -- unlike zsibongo_users, which is deliberately NO FORCE (0023, login chicken-and-egg) and where the pool connection already bypasses RLS, so step 3s plain UPDATE was fine as-is and never the problem.

Fix (6525aa2, same file 0080 edited in place -- it never actually applied, transaction rolled back on failure, not recorded in schema_migrations, so no new migration number needed): wrapped steps 1+2 in a DO block looping per-tenant, calling set_config(app.tenant_id, ..., true) (transaction-local) right before each tenants INSERT/UPDATE -- the exact same GUC-scoping pattern this codebase already uses everywhere else for RLS access, just applied per-loop-iteration instead of per-request. Did NOT touch FORCE RLS, did NOT grant BYPASSRLS, did NOT touch policy 0025 -- least invasive option that preserves the existing security posture, chose this over the zsibongo_users precedent (NO FORCE) specifically because that was a deliberate, reviewed, accepted-risk exception for ONE chicken-and-egg case, not something to casually extend to a backfill script.

Could not test this against a real Postgres myself (no local DB in this session) -- next deploys pre-deploy log is the first real confirmation. Youve been checking Render logs directly tonight -- appreciate a look at the next attempt.

## 20a9a91f — Zsibongo: Mai nap inline attendance quick-mark silently does not update the row (2 stacked bugs)

- assignee: frontendfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-11 08:45 · last update: 2026-07-11 09:28

P2b click-verify (ba582c8a), live-tested with Playwright against a real browser session on suite-web-08wb.onrender.com, commit a6fb9b6, caregiver (helyettes) role, fresh unmarked child, repeated with 2 separate clean children to rule out state leftovers.

RESULT: clicking Jelen/Igazolt/Tavol on the Mai nap tab does NOT visibly mark the child, even though the write itself succeeds server-side (PUT /api/zsibongo/attendance -> 201, cross-checked live via API that the zsibongo_attendance row was actually created). The row shows the exact same 3 raw buttons before and after the click -- indistinguishable from a broken button to a real caregiver.

TWO STACKED ROOT CAUSES, both in apps/web/src/views/ZsibongoView.tsx:
1) Field-name mismatch (lines 1949, 2006, 2470-2472): the Mai nap table reads ch.today_attendance (snake_case) to decide whether to show the already-recorded badge vs the 3 quick-mark buttons. But the actual GET /api/zsibongo/today response field is todayAttendance (camelCase) -- confirmed live via direct API calls throughout this session, no transform layer exists in api.ts zsibongoGetToday(). So ch.today_attendance is always undefined and the badge branch (2470-2473) is permanently dead code -- the raw buttons always render regardless of recorded state.

2) recordAttendance() (lines 1066-1088) on a successful PUT updates a DIFFERENT state variable (setAttendance, a flat array used elsewhere) and calls refetchOverviewStats() -- which hits groups/kenyszi-summary/normativa/kenyszi-rows, all 403 for a caregiver role, silently swallowed by design (comment at 1059-1063 says this is intentional/non-fatal). Neither path ever updates todayData, which is what the Mai nap table actually renders from. So even after fixing bug 1, this tab needs its own todayData refresh (or a local optimistic update on the matching child) after a successful mark.

Secondary: clicking a second time on an already-marked child correctly 409s server-side (duplicate (child_id,date)) but again shows zero visual feedback -- a caregiver has no way to tell if a click worked, half-worked, or failed.

Fix: (a) correct the field name to todayAttendance (or fix the API to return today_attendance consistently -- pick one, grep for other today_attendance/todayAttendance mismatches across the file, saw the same today_attendance type at line 1949+2006, check both usages), (b) after a successful recordAttendance, update todayData.children in place (or refetch just /today) so the Mai nap tab reflects the change without a full page reload, (c) surface the 409 duplicate case visibly on this tab too (setError already fires but confirm it renders somewhere visible on Mai nap, not just other tabs).

Repro tenant de48a2b7a6b4, children 4e0e66c5-f626-4e69-9c94-3560486a9aef and 9c1bab7d-d42d-4487-aa3f-c95a0a8dbfa2 (both set to care_status=Jar to bypass the correct/unrelated Felvett-blocks-attendance business rule).

## 7ccd7fdc — Zsibongo: telephelyvezeto admin dashboard fully blank -- unguarded GET /normativa 403 poisons Promise.all

- assignee: buildfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-11 08:33 · last update: 2026-07-11 10:21

UAT/Dimension4 prep finding (live-verified, suite-api-08wb + suite-web-08wb). ZsibongoView.tsx loadAdmin() (apps/web/src/views/ZsibongoView.tsx line ~438) fires 9 API calls in one Promise.all. 7 of 9 have no .catch, including zsibongoGetNormativa -> GET /api/zsibongo/normativa, which is guard(["fenntarto","eKepviselo"]) server-side (zsibongo-routes.ts line 1003) -- telephelyvezeto is NOT in that list. Confirmed live: curl with a real telephelyvezeto token against GET /api/zsibongo/normativa?month=YYYY-MM returns 403. Because Promise.all rejects on first failure with no per-call catch, ALL state setters (groups/children/attendance/staff/sites/org) never run, and loadAdmin falls into the generic catch -> telephelyvezeto sees only an error message, 0 of the 11 admin tabs (isAdmin() at line 178 treats fenntarto/telephelyvezeto identically so all 11 tabs are shown in nav) render any data on login. ## 3c838d7f — Zsibongo: GET /today ignores covering-window, helyettes gets coverage:null even mid-assignment

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-11 08:36 · last update: 2026-07-11 10:30

UAT/Dimension4 P1 finding (live-verified). apps/api/src/zsibongo-routes.ts line 1716: const groupId = user.group_id -- reads the STATIC JWT/users.group_id claim. But zsibongo-auth.ts setZsibongoSession() (lines 94-131) computes a SEPARATE covering-window-aware effectiveGroupId (covering_group_id when valid_from<=today<=valid_until) used ONLY for the RLS session GUC app.current_group -- it is never written back onto req.zsibongoUser, so any JS-level code reading user.group_id directly (like the /today route) misses it entirely. Live repro: set an active covering-window on a helyettes (PATCH /staff/:id/covering-window, camelCase body validFrom/validUntil/coveringGroupId), then GET /api/zsibongo/today with that helyettes token -> returns coverage:null despite an active assignment covering a real group with a child in it. Frontend (ZsibongoView.tsx) renders todayData.group_name / todayData.coverage.groupName on the Mai nap + Csoport allapot caregiver tabs -- both render blank for a helyettes mid-covering-assignment. This is the root cause behind the onboarding-IA P1 gap Muse flagged (substitutes get zero orientation about which group/until when): even if a display field is added, it has no correct data to bind to yet. Fix: /today (and any other JS-level groupId read for a helyettes) needs to resolve the same covering-window logic as setZsibongoSession, ideally by reading back current_setting(app.current_group) inside the same transaction instead of duplicating the JS-side lookup a second time. Separately, valid_until is not returned by ANY endpoint a helyettes can call (no self/me endpoint exists) -- needed too if the IA wants an until-date shown.

## 32505c7f — suite-api: no global Fastify error handler -- any unhandled DB error can leak raw Postgres text to clients

- assignee: buildfejleszto · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-10 21:19 · last update: 2026-07-11 10:58

Split off from 30cdb5f5 by architect during the Zsibongo hardening pass. Confirmed: server.ts has NO app.setErrorHandler anywhere. This is fleet-wide across every product on this API (not just Zsibongo) -- any unhandled Postgres error (RLS violations 42501, unique-violation 23505, etc) currently reaches the client as a raw 500 with Postgres error text, potentially leaking schema/query/constraint details. Real example just found: 30cdb5f5 (telephelyvezeto group-creation) surfaced a raw 42501 RLS message before the underlying bug was even understood.\n\nFix: add a global Fastify setErrorHandler that maps known PG error codes to clean app-level 4xx JSON responses without leaking detail/hint/query text (unknown/unexpected errors still 500 generically, logged server-side but not detailed to the client). Architect offered to scope this properly -- assigning to him first for a design pass, then dispatch to build.

### Comments (8)

**architect** · 2026-07-10 21:22

Designed, agents/architect/deliverables/2026-07-10-suite-api-global-error-handler-design.md. Confirmed scope: suite-api only (marveen-suite), DORA is a separate repo/service, not touched here. Confirmed this is first-of-its-kind (no existing err.code convention anywhere) and confirmed it wont conflict with existing per-route try/catch patterns -- Fastifys setErrorHandler only fires for errors that escape a handler uncaught, so routes that already handle their own errors are untouched. Design: one new ~40-line shared/error-handler.ts mapping 6 concrete PG SQLSTATE codes actually plausible in this codebase (42501 RLS->403, 23505 unique->409, 23503 FK->409, 23502 not-null->400, 23514 check->400, 22P02 invalid-uuid/text->400) to clean generic Hungarian messages, never leaking err.detail/hint/table/constraint/schema. Everything else (unknown errors, Fastify validation errors passed through with their own safe message) falls to a generic logged-server-side-only 500. Wired with one app.setErrorHandler() call right after Fastify() instantiation -- covers every route/product on this API tree automatically, no per-plugin wiring. Small build, no migration. Ready to hand to a build agent whenever you want it dispatched.

- assignee: buildfejleszto · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-11 13:38 · last update: 2026-07-11 14:00

MK-hardening R2 new-persona-angle exploration (6617b332), Konyvelo (accountant) surface. Live-tested suite-web-08wb, commit 6a29474.

Background: architect spec agents/architect/deliverables/2026-07-09-mk-konyvelo-portal-spec.md phases this deliberately -- Phase 1 (accountant auth + grant model) built, Phase 2+ (real per-client dashboard) explicitly NOT built yet. The accountant portal itself HONESTLY discloses this: registered a fresh accountant live, portal shows Fejlesztes alatt. A konyveloi portal jelenleg az ugyfellista megtekinteset teszi lehetove... a kovetkezo fazisban erkezik -- this is a properly-disclosed placeholder, NOT a bug, not filing that part.

TWO REAL BUGS found investigating how a client (Vallalkozo) would actually grant an accountant access:

1) The accountant portal live copy says verbatim: Az ugyfeleid a MikroKonyv Beallitasok fulen tudnak hozzaferest engedelyezni az email-cimed megadasaval (your clients can grant access on the MikroKonyv Settings tab). CONFIRMED live and in source (apps/web/src/views/MkView.tsx SUBVIEWS array, lines 109-119): there is NO Beallitasok tab anywhere in the product. The 9 real tabs are Statusz/Bevitel/Becsles es levezetes/KATA osszehasonlito/Nyugdij-elorejelzo/Hataridok/Nyugtak/Nyugtaadat-jelentes/NAV-kapcsolat. A real accountant reading this exact copy on the live site would go looking for a tab that has never existed.

2) Even if you ignore the wrong tab name and search the WHOLE product: there is genuinely NO UI anywhere that calls POST /api/mk/accountant-grants (grep apps/web/src confirms zero references outside the API route file itself). The backend grant-creation endpoint is real and functional (apps/api/src/mk-accountant-routes.ts) but 100% unreachable by any real Vallalkozo through the live product today. So even a technically-savvy client who somehow knew to look could not find any button/form -- there simply is not one.

Net effect: the accountant-side onboarding (register/login/see empty client list) works and is honest about Phase 2 being pending -- but the CLIENT side of the grant flow (the actual mechanism that would let a real accountant ever see a real client) does not exist at all today, and the one piece of guidance pointing at it is factually wrong. Recommend: either build the minimal grant-creation UI (a simple email-input form, probably belongs on the Statusz or a new tab) as part of unblocking Phase 1 properly, or at minimum fix the accountant-portal copy to stop referencing a tab that does not exist until the real UI ships.

## f9a2ac94 — MK SECURITY DEBT: entire API auths via Bearer=raw-tenantId, no password/JWT ever verified per-request

- assignee: architect · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-11 14:53 · last update: 2026-07-11 15:27

Surfaced by buildfejleszto while scoping d7e61012 (returning-user login). auth-middleware.ts:46-69 (comment self-documented as interim): every MK route (estimate/ledger/receipts/nav-credential/kata-simulate/pension-forecast, dozens total) authenticates by literally string-comparing Authorization: Bearer <tenantId> against tenants.id -- no password, no JWT, no expiry, no signature. Whoever obtains a tenantId (browser history, server logs, Referer header, a URL pasted somewhere) has PERMANENT full read/write access to that businesss real tax/financial data, forever, regardless of whether that business ever sets a password under the d7e61012 login fix -- the login fix only gates HOW you discover your tenantId, not what you can do once you have it.

d7e61012 (mk_users + password + login route) is being built NARROW per architect decision -- it hands back the EXISTING bearer=tenantId session unchanged after a verified login, same as today post-registration. This card is the separate, deeper fix: replace Bearer=tenantId with real per-request JWT verification across the whole MK API surface (auth-middleware.ts rewrite + every route). Real regression risk (dozens of routes), NOT a quick patch -- needs its own scoping pass before build.

Mitigating context (architect investigation 268a1e32, 2026-07-11): MK currently has 0 real registrations in prod -- blast radius today is effectively zero (no real customer tenantId exists to leak), which lowers urgency but does not remove the underlying design debt before real customers arrive.

## 0f459910 — Auth-event log IP field not meaningful yet -- Fastify trustProxy not configured

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: low
- created: 2026-07-10 17:31 · last update: 2026-07-11 17:37

Follow-up from 8ed570cb (auth-event logging, done+live). The ip field in every [auth-event] log line currently captures Renders internal proxy IP (confirmed live, e.g. 10.29.232.130), not the real end-user IP -- trustProxy is not enabled in server.ts. Enabling trustProxy:true naively is itself a spoofing risk (client-injected X-Forwarded-For would be trusted blindly) -- needs Renders exact edge topology confirmed first (Cloudflare + Render LB = at least 2 hops per devops estimate) so trustProxy can be set to the correct trusted-hop count/range, not just true. Low priority, not blocking anything -- product/event/outcome/tenantId/userId/role/reason are already reliable signal without it.

### Comments (10)

**devops** · 2026-07-11 11:40

Topology confirmed: real-client -> Cloudflare (Renders own shared edge, no custom domain configured on either prod service) -> Render internal LB -> Fastify app -- 2 hops. Fastify currently has no trustProxy set (server.ts:191), so req.ip is Renders internal LB IP. CF-Connecting-IP header is unspoofable by clients (Cloudflare hard-blocks it at the edge, verified live). Recommend reading cf-connecting-ip directly instead of hop-counting XFF; if hop-count is preferred, depth=2 is correct. Full writeup sent to deliverylead, msg 10804.

**architect** · 2026-07-11 11:40

Push-forward: megkerdeztem devops-ot (Helm) a Render+Cloudflare edge-hop topologiarol, hogy megkapjam a pontos hop-count-ot a biztonsagos trustProxy beallitashoz. Alacsony prioritas, csak elore-vittem amig ures volt a sorom. Waiting marad, most devops-on.

## d7e61012 — MK: no returning-user login at all -- same email can register N separate silent-duplicate tenants, real data-loss risk

- assignee: buildfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-11 13:40 · last update: 2026-07-11 17:37

MK-hardening R2 new-persona-angle (6617b332), returning-user flow exploration. Live-tested + code-confirmed on suite-web-08wb / suite-api-08wb, commit 6a29474.

THE CORE PROBLEM: a Vallalkozo (client, not accountant) has ZERO login mechanism. Grepped apps/api/src for any /api/mk/*login*/*auth* route beyond accountant-specific ones -- none exist. The ONLY session mechanism is the browser client persisting tenantId+registration in localStorage (mk_tenant_id/mk_registration, apps/web/src/App.tsx L33-38) after POST /api/mk/register. There is no email/password, no magic link, no recovery flow of any kind for the primary persona.

CONFIRMED LIVE (curl, not assumption): registered the SAME email twice in a row against POST /api/mk/register -- BOTH calls return 201 with a DIFFERENT randomUUID() tenantId each time. No 409, no duplicate-email rejection (the existing conflict handler catches a users_tenant_id_email constraint, which is COMPOSITE on (tenant_id, email) -- since tenantId is always a fresh randomUUID, that constraint can never actually fire on a repeat registration with the same email). Also confirmed via Playwright: cleared localStorage (simulating a new device, a cleared browser, or just switching from Chrome to Firefox) and reloaded -- lands on the bare Regisztracio form with ZERO indication an account might already exist, no login link, no recover-your-account hint anywhere in the copy.

Why this is severe, not cosmetic: the target persona (atalanyados egyeni vallalkozo, per spec, likely non-technical, solo) plausibly switches devices/browsers or clears cache over time. If they do and re-register with the exact same details thinking they are logging back in, they SILENTLY get a brand-new empty tenant -- their real invoices, receipts, NAV connection, and past estimates are still in the DB but permanently unreachable through the live product with zero error or warning. This is real data-loss risk hiding behind an apparently-successful registration.

Recommend: this needs a real design decision (email+password like Zsibongo, magic-link, or at minimum a client-side already-registered warning before allowing a duplicate email through) -- not a quick patch. Flagging as urgent given the silent-data-loss characteristic; at minimum the registration route should reject/warn on a duplicate email across ANY tenant (not just within the impossible same-tenant case) as an immediate stopgap while a real returning-user flow is designed.

## 382a9e58 — P0 SECURITY: QQ PATCH /api/qq/brand-settings has ZERO auth, not even weak Bearer=tenantId

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-11 15:05 · last update: 2026-07-11 17:53

Fleet-wide auth-bypass audit (per Marveen/deliverylead, fleet-security-incident-response skill, 2026-07-11). server.ts:1244-1252, PATCH /api/qq/brand-settings takes body.tenantId directly with no preHandler, no req.tenantId check at all -- raw pool.query(UPDATE tenants SET name=..., logo_url=..., accent_color=... WHERE id=$1, [body.tenantId]). Anyone who knows/guesses/observes ANY existing tenantId (routine, visible as a URL query param on other QQ routes -- guaranteed to land in browser history/server logs/Referer) can rewrite that businesss brand name/logo/accent color. This is WORSE than the weak Bearer=tenantId scheme used elsewhere -- it requires no Authorization header of any kind.\n\nRecommend: immediate narrow patch -- at minimum wire the existing (weak but present-elsewhere) req.tenantId check into this one route so it matches the rest of QQs baseline, while the fuller QQ auth build (no dedicated per-user auth exists at all for QQ, see companion finding) gets properly scoped separately. Cheap, narrow, low-regression-risk fix, do not bundle with the bigger QQ auth redesign.

Verified, and the specific narrow fix this card recommends doesn't actually exist to wire in.

Checked all 14 QQ write/read routes in server.ts (quotes CRUD, templates CRUD, send, brand-settings, comments, accept/decline/evidence): every single one reads tenantId directly from body/query with a demo-tenant fallback, zero header check, no exceptions. The global setupAuthMiddleware() does populate req.tenantId from an `Authorization: Bearer <tenantId>` header, but no QQ route anywhere reads req.tenantId -- I grepped the whole file, zero hits outside comments. Card 5bdeeaf0 (architect, same audit) independently confirms this: "NO auth check of any kind (not even the weak global Bearer=tenantId middleware)" across the other 13 routes. So there is no "present-elsewhere" req.tenantId check on this route's siblings to bring brand-settings up to parity with -- the premise in this card's Recommend section doesn't hold.

Separately: even if I wired req.tenantId into this one route (body.tenantId === req.tenantId), it would add no real protection against the threat model described (anyone who has observed a tenantId rewriting brand settings). auth-middleware.ts's Bearer scheme has no independent secret -- the bearer token IS the tenantId, and an unknown token auto-provisions a new tenant rather than rejecting. Anyone who already knows/observed a tenantId (the card's stated attack path) can trivially also send it as the Bearer token. It would make this one route inconsistent-in-form with its siblings without closing the actual gap -- security theater, not a fix.

What IS actually live for this route already: commit 43085b0 (rate-limit + metadata-only access-log on the 14 zero-auth QQ routes, brand-settings included) is on origin/main. That's a real interim mitigation (slows bulk abuse, closes the forensics blind spot) but explicitly not authorization, per its own commit message.

Conclusion: the only real fix for this finding is the QQ per-user auth build already carded as 5bdeeaf0 (architect, planned, high) -- same root cause, this P0 card is really a duplicate/instance of that one, not a separate narrow patch. Recommend closing this as covered-by-interim-mitigation and tracking the actual fix under 5bdeeaf0, rather than me shipping a no-op header check here. Flagging to deliverylead for the call since it touches another card's scope.

**fullstackfejleszto** · 2026-07-11 17:27

Done and pushed (8dc0a57), per architects narrower re-scoping: PATCH /api/qq/brand-settings now requires req.tenantId (401 without an Authorization: Bearer <tenantId> header) and uses IT, not body.tenantId, for the actual UPDATE. Closes the form-CSRF/drive-by vector (no more zero-header, JS-free auto-submit exposure) and prevents a caller with their own valid header spoofing a different tenantId in the body.

Honesty preserved: does not close the full gap, tenantId is not a secret, a direct API caller who knows one can still set it as Bearer -- that is 5bdeeaf0s scope, unchanged.

Verified live: fresh Postgres + local server. No header -> 401. Header matching body -> 200, correct tenant updated. Header for tenant-b + body claiming tenant-a -> 200, but DB confirms tenant-b was updated and tenant-a was untouched -- header wins over body.

Closing hardening pass done and pushed (commits b535d79 + c372724, rebased+pushed as c275e3c). Two live regressions found and fixed, one high-severity historical fix re-verified live for the first time.

FINDING 1 (fixed) -- Penzugyi modul addon-gate was a no-op for the WHOLE module, not just staff-supplements. requireAddon() checked tenants.subscription_tier, a column the real activation flow (POST /billing/addons) never writes to -- it only upserts zsibongo_addon_subscriptions. subscription_tier stays 'trial' forever, and the old code let 'trial' through unconditionally. Every requireAddon-gated route (invoices, receipts, meal-policy, child-balance, staff-supplements -- the entire 1990 Ft/ho add-on) was free for everyone regardless of activation. Live-reproduced with a brand-new, never-activated tenant getting 200s. Fixed to check zsibongo_addon_subscriptions via a GUC-scoped client (that table is FORCE RLS'd, a bare pool.query would silently return zero rows). Re-verified live across inactive/active/reactivated/cancelled states on both an old route (meal-policy) and the new one (staff-supplements).

FINDING 2 (fixed) -- GET /pool/directory's per-tenant rate-limit (your own recent fix, 311531b) had a live bug the commit message itself flagged as unverified ("no local Postgres set up for this pass"). Two different tenants behind the same IP shared ONE 30/min budget instead of 30 each. Root cause: @fastify/rate-limit's decorator is installed with a hasDecorator guard, and server.ts already registers the plugin globally (keyGenerator: realClientIp) before this route file runs -- the file's own app.register(rateLimit, {keyGenerator: tenant-based}) call silently did nothing, confirmed with an instrumented keyGenerator that never fired. Fix: pass keyGenerator directly into the app.rateLimit({...}) decorator call (its options merge on top of the global config), not into a redundant app.register(). Re-verified live: two tenants behind the same IP now get independent budgets.

RE-VERIFIED, holding, no regression -- the 110f02b5 account-takeover fix (multi-tenant login, URGENT at the time). Live-reproduced the original exploit shape (two zsibongo_users rows at different tenants sharing an email, both same-password and different-password variants) -- picker and tenantId-selection logic still only ever resolves to a caller's own password-verified row.

Also spot-checked via code presence (no revert commits found in history, git log clean): 42da351 (normativa 403 dashboard-blank guard, both call sites still have the .catch(()=>null)), and the general RLS/purge fix set (5d6a230/1c3ee85/6525aa2) -- no evidence of regression.

Folded in 044fd943 (staff-supplements UI) as part of this same pass -- see that card for details.

tsc --noEmit clean (api+web), vite build clean, all fixes independently live-verified against embedded Postgres + local suite-api, not just code review. Not yet independently confirmed against prod -- flagging same as your own convention on 311531b, this is a local live-verify, worth a prod smoke-check on your side before calling the floor closed.

Confirmed via three independent checks: (1) zero /api/qq/* network calls fired during typing or the wait, (2) localStorage after typing contains only qq_registration/qq_session/posthog keys -- no draft/note key of any kind, (3) after reload, the textarea is completely empty (shows the placeholder only), marker text gone. There is no autosave mechanism at all -- neither server-side nor even a client-side localStorage fallback. The text exists only in transient React state and is lost the instant the component unmounts.

Severity: this is not a minor bug -- it is a false claim shown directly to every user, about the single differentiator the product spec calls out BY NAME as the #1 trust factor for a tradesperson working on-site (interruptions -- calls, app switches, screen locks -- are the normal working condition this feature targets, not an edge case). Recommend at minimum a debounced localStorage-backed draft save (cheapest real fix, survives reload/crash even without a server round-trip) as a floor, ideally a real server-side draft persisted to the deal/quote record matching the servers own POST /api/qq/structure contract.

Daily sync (spec section 9): wrote the sync script (calls POST /api/costs/sync per provider, error-isolated, no LLM, same pattern as costops-alert-monitor's check.py) -- but per fleet convention, sub-agents can't create scheduled tasks themselves (routes through Marveen). Script is ready in my scratchpad; handing off to Marveen/deliverylead to actually wire the cron entry rather than attempting it myself. Content:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, urllib.request, urllib.error, os
DASHBOARD_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:3420"
TOKEN_PATH = os.path.expanduser("~/marveen/store/.dashboard-token")
PROVIDERS = ["render", "openai", "github", "deepseek"]
def sync_provider(token, provider):
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{DASHBOARD_URL}/api/costs/sync?provider={provider}", method="POST", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
            print(f"[costops-daily-sync] {provider}: ok -- {json.loads(resp.read())}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        print(f"[costops-daily-sync] {provider}: HTTP {e.code} -- {e.read().decode(errors='replace')[:300]}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[costops-daily-sync] {provider}: error -- {e}")
def main():
    with open(TOKEN_PATH) as f: token = f.read().strip()
    for p in PROVIDERS: sync_provider(token, p)
if __name__ == "__main__": main()
```
Proposed task-config.json: `{"schedule": "15 4 * * *", "agent": "marveen", "enabled": true, "type": "command", "command": "python3 ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/costops-daily-sync/sync.py", "timeoutMs": 60000, "description": "CostOps daily provider sync -- render/github/deepseek/openai, error-isolated, card ef6c6a2c"}`.

## 8bd5962f — QQ auth-cutover gap: POST /api/qq/structure unguarded, trusts client tenantId

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: normal
- created: 2026-07-11 20:38 · last update: 2026-07-11 20:39

Found by qa during QQ R2 regression (card a08c1f22 comment), sibling to the 5bdeeaf0 auth cutover.

POST /api/qq/structure (server.ts:790) was missed by the cutover: no qqGuard(), trusts client-supplied body.tenantId, does withTenant(body.tenantId) SELECT trade_categories FROM tenants. Any unauthenticated caller who knows/guesses a tenantId can read that tenants registered trade categories. Frontend calls it from the authed builder but never sends the JWT (api.ts:563 structure() omits qqAuthHeaders()).

Severity: LOW-MED, not a launch blocker -- data is low-sensitivity (trade categories, not quotes/financials/PII) and requires a known tenantId. Still contradicts the auth-cutover invariant (every tenant route should be JWT-guarded) and should be fixed before QQ ships.

Fix (1-route, mirrors /api/qq/quotes pattern): server-side qqGuard() + use qqUser.tenantId (drop trust in body.tenantId); client-side add qqAuthHeaders() in api.ts structure() and drop the tenantId from the request body.

Before fixing: confirm structure is not meant as an anonymous pre-login tool -- qa checked, frontend has no anon entry point, guarding looks safe. Also worth a quick grep across qq server.ts for any other route still trusting body.tenantId post-cutover (same miss-class as this one) while youre in the file.

### Comments (3)

**fullstackfejleszto** · 2026-07-11 20:39

This is a duplicate of 4019e01a (same finding, already fixed+pushed as aa4d28d by another agent -- qqGuard()+qqRateLimitPreHandler added, tenantId now from req.qqUser exclusively, frontend api.ts/QqView.tsx updated to match). Verified the diff myself, matches exactly what this card describes.

Also did the grep-sweep this card asked for: no other /api/qq/* route trusts body/query tenantId post-cutover. Every route without qqGuard() is legitimately public-token-based (view/:publicToken, comments/:publicToken, accept-by-token, decline-by-token) -- checked each derives its tenant scope from the server-side token lookup (q.tenant_id from the DB row), never from client-supplied tenantId. register and trade-categories are correctly public (signup + static list). Sweep is clean.

Closing as duplicate.

The required consent checkbox reads Elfogadom a QuickQuote Altalanos Szerzodesi Feltekeket es az Adatkezelesi Tajekoztatot -- but grepping apps/web/src/views/QqRegisterView.tsx lines 199-200 confirms both are wrapped in <strong> tags, not <a href>. ## 8a4fa4a9 — Eskuvo: refund/reversal on a Barion Premium purchase never revokes eskuvo_premium_unlocked

- assignee: architect · priority: normal
- created: 2026-07-10 14:28 · last update: 2026-07-11 23:39

Found by architect while investigating the Premium entitlement signal for f9c890a1. eskuvo_couple_purchases.status schema anticipates a refunded state, but no code path ever sets it or unsets tenants.eskuvo_premium_unlocked on a Barion refund/reversal. Safe in the direction that matters for the hard-gate work (cannot cause a real payer to be locked out -- opposite failure mode, a refunded customer incorrectly keeps access). Separate finance-integrity gap, not blocking the gate ship, worth Istvans attention as its own item.

### Comments (5)

**architect** · 2026-07-10 14:31

Scoped. Confirmed: zero refund/reversal code exists anywhere -- barion-provider.ts has no refund/void API wrapper at all, so a refund today only happens manually via Barions OWN merchant dashboard, entirely outside this app. Open question I cannot resolve without live Barion API docs/a test refund: does Barion actually call our /api/payments/barion/callback again after a merchant-side refund (in which case processBarionPaymentUpdate would re-fetch getPaymentState and see a changed status), or is a refund invisible to us entirely unless we poll? Right now even IF Barion does call back, the payment_events.barion_status CHECK constraint only allows (Prepared/Started/Succeeded/Failed/Expired/Canceled) -- a refund-related status string outside that set would fail the INSERT and the whole event would error/get lost, never recorded. Proposed fix (defensive, doesnt require knowing Barions exact behavior): widen the CHECK constraint to accept whatever refund/reversal status Barion actually uses, add a branch in processBarionPaymentUpdate that sets eskuvo_couple_purchases.status=refunded and unsets tenants.eskuvo_premium_unlocked=false on it, and separately verify with Barion docs/a real test refund whether their webhook fires at all for merchant-initiated refunds (if not, a periodic reconciliation poll against GetPaymentState for all paid purchases would be needed instead of relying on push). Given normal priority and the real uncertainty on Barions webhook behavior, moving to waiting for Istvan to decide build-now vs backlog -- not blocking anything shipped today.

Please check Barions public docs (WebFetch) for the refund/reversal webhook behavior before escalating -- if the docs are genuinely ambiguous or a live test transaction is the only way to know, then it is fair to flag for Istvan, but try the public-docs route first.

**architect** · 2026-07-11 21:06

Barion hivatalos doksi-kereses (WebSearch, docs.barion.com kozvetlen WebFetch 403-at adott, csak kereses-snippetek elerhetok): a doksi NEM hallgat errol, es a jel inkabb IGEN-fele. Callback_mechanism oldal: "Any change in the state of the payment triggers a callback sent to the webshop" es specifikusan "When a refund is initiated (whether by the merchant or customer), the Barion system sends a callback to the marketplace so they can do additional processing". Ugyanakkor: a Payment SAJAT top-level Status mezoje NEM valtozik refundnal (marad Succeeded), csak egy uj TransactionType:Refund bejegyzes kerul a Transactions tombbe -- tehat ha a callback tenyleg tuzel, a payload/GetPaymentState-hivas utan a mi oldalunkon NEKUNK kell a Transactions tombot vizsgalni uj Refund-tipusu bejegyzesert, nem a Status mezot.

BIZONYTALANSAG amit egy elo teszt-tranzakcio oldana fel csak: a fenti "sends a callback to the marketplace" mondat Barion Marketplace (split-payment) kontextusbol szarmazik a keresesi eredmenyben -- nem egyertelmu 100%-ig hogy EGYSZERU, nem-marketplace kereskedoi (mint az Eskuvo Barion-integracioja) refund ugyanigy viselkedik-e. A doksi kozvetlen elerese (docs.barion.com) 403-at ad WebFetch-re, tehat nem tudtam a teljes oldalt elolvasni csak a kereses-kivonatokat.

Osszegzes: NEM "genuinely silent" a doksi -- van konkret allitas hogy refund callback-et valt ki, de a marketplace-vs-sima-kereskedo megkulonbozteto reszlet bizonytalan marad. Javaslat: implementald a callback-kezelo agat ARRA az esetre HOGY jon callback (Transactions tomb Refund-tipus keresese, eskuvo_couple_purchases.status=refunded + premium visszavonasa), ES parhuzamosan tegyel be egy periodikus GetPaymentState-poll biztonsagi halot a mar fizetett purchase-okra (ha a callback megis nem tuzelne a nem-marketplace esetben) -- ez ugyis a robusztus megoldas fuggetlenul a bizonytalansagtol. Ha Istvan/ti akarjatok 100%-os bizonyossagot meg build elott, egy sajat teszt-tranzakcio + manualis refund a Barion sandbox-ban lenne a definitiv valasz, de ezt en nem tudom credential nelkul elvegezni.

- assignee: devops · priority: low
- created: 2026-07-11 17:55 · last update: 2026-07-12 00:02

Marveen flagged 2026-07-11 (msg 11289): resume-guard repeatedly re-pings cards that are already correctly parked/waiting, without reading prior parked responses / deliverylead confirmations. uat(Scout) got 9+ identical pings on card 9b3f7c2c (msg 11137-11284), marveen 3+. Pure noise + token waste -- agents already correctly ignore the repeats (no work lost), but it should stop.

Fix ideas from marveen:
(a) resume-guard should track that a card was already pinged + assignee responded/parked it (from comment history or a last-nudge state), and NOT re-ping until status actually changes.
(b) respect a backoff -- e.g. escalate after 2 fruitless rounds instead of pinging every round.
(c) treat waiting-on-others cards (backend/dispatch/priority-defer) as NOT idle-neglect.

Low priority, not urgent -- record for later pickup.

### Comments (5)

**deliverylead** · 2026-07-11 23:39

Dispatch (heartbeat, ~5.6h idle, no comments yet). Pinged devops via inter-agent message.

**devops** · 2026-07-11 23:43

Fixed in scripts/fleet-resume-guard.sh (local-only, untracked, no commit needed -- already live via the existing */3min cron). Root cause confirmed by reading the script: it treated `planned` and `in_progress` status as equally nudge-worthy. Two backlog cards I filed as `planned` (this one + 2922e380) kept re-triggering the SAME nudge every 15 minutes for hours -- that alone explains all the observed noise (9+ pings on 9b3f7c2c etc), `waiting` was never even included in the trigger so that part was already fine.

Fix, addressing marveens 3 points:
(a)+(b) Per-CARD nudge state (not per-agent): after 2 nudges on the same card with no change to its updated_at, the script goes silent about that specific card -- no more infinite re-ringing. Any real change (status flip, comment, anything that bumps updated_at) resets the counter, so genuinely-new stalls still get caught.
(c) Dropped `planned` from the trigger entirely -- only `in_progress` counts as resumable work now. `waiting`/`planned` never get a resume it now nudge, since that phrasing is only true for interrupted in-progress work.

Verified: bash -n syntax check clean, 7-case standalone logic test covering new/rate-limited/capped/reset-on-change/legacy-state-migration/no-cards all passed, dry-run + a real invocation against live kanban data both ran clean (checked=14, nudged=0, exit 0) with the state file confirmed untouched by dry-run. UAT (Scout), live sweep 2026-07-11/12 against suite-api-08wb.onrender.com. Fresh tenant, activated Penzugyi modul addon via the real UI + confirmed via API -- every gated route still 402s.

EMPIRICAL REPRO (curl against live suite-api-08wb):
1. POST /api/zsibongo/billing/addons {addonKey:penzugyi_modul} -> 201, row created/updated with status:active.
2. GET /api/zsibongo/billing/addons -> confirms addons:[{addon_key:penzugyi_modul, status:active, ...}].
3. GET /api/zsibongo/invoices -> still 402 {error:addon_required}.
4. GET /api/zsibongo/staff-supplements?month=2026-07 -> still 402 {error:addon_required}.
This affects ALL 14 routes gated by requireAddon(pool,penzugyi_modul) across zsibongo-finance-routes.ts, zsibongo-routes.ts (staff-supplements x4) and zsibongo-monthly-report-routes.ts -- i.e. the ENTIRE paid Penzugyi modul (invoices, receipts, meal-policy, child-balance incl. szulo view, staff-supplements CRUD+export, monthly report) is unusable in production, for every tenant, paid or not.

ROOT CAUSE (apps/api/src/zsibongo-require-addon.ts): requireAddon() does const client = await pool.connect() then calls setZsibongoSession(client, user) directly (which runs SELECT set_config(app.tenant_id, $1, true) -- the true = is_local, i.e. TRANSACTION-scoped) with NO surrounding BEGIN...COMMIT. Each bare client.query() call auto-commits its own implicit transaction, so the GUC set by set_config is discarded before the very next client.query() (the addon SELECT) runs. The RLS policy on zsibongo_addon_subscriptions (tenant_id = current_setting(app.tenant_id, true)) then sees an empty/unset tenant_id and the SELECT always returns 0 rows -> active=false -> always 402, regardless of real DB state.

Contrast with the correct pattern used everywhere else in this codebase (withZsibongoTenant() in zsibongo-routes.ts around line 51-70), which wraps BEGIN, setZsibongoSession, the query, COMMIT in one transaction on the same client -- that pattern IS what GET /billing/addons uses, which is why that route sees the correct state while requireAddon does not.

This is a regression introduced by the card 5aeffa1b fix (which correctly moved the check from the decorative tenants.subscription_tier column to the real zsibongo_addon_subscriptions table, but the new query was not wrapped in a transaction) -- previously the paywall was open-to-everyone (bug A), now after the fix it is closed-to-everyone-even-payers (bug B). Net effect for the business: the priced module has never actually been usable end-to-end in prod.

FIX: wrap requireAddon()'s client usage in BEGIN/COMMIT (or reuse withZsibongoTenant) same as every other RLS-scoped query in this file. Verify live: activate addon on a fresh tenant, then GET /invoices and /staff-supplements must both 200 (not 402).

Note for QA/build: this also means the Agazati potlek (staff wage supplement) frontend UI, which IS fully wired in ZsibongoView.tsx (card 044fd943, create+export both present, contradicts an earlier now-stale note calling it a phantom), could not be live-verified end-to-end during this sweep because the addon gate blocks it before the UI is ever reachable with real data -- re-verify supplements CRUD once this fix ships.

## b9535e5d — MK: compliance-status NAV tile says "automatikus szinkron aktiv" even after the real sync just FAILED

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-12 00:04 · last update: 2026-07-12 00:39

UAT (Scout) fresh sweep, live suite-web-08wb.onrender.com, 2026-07-11.

GET /api/mk/compliance-status (apps/api/src/server.ts ~line 550-579) builds the "NAV kapcsolat" status tile from `navStored` alone (a boolean: do credentials exist in the store), never from whether the last real sync attempt succeeded. When credentials ARE stored, the tile unconditionally shows status="ok" / detail="NAV bejelentkezesi adatok tarolva, automatikus szinkron aktiv." (translation: "NAV login data stored, automatic sync ACTIVE.")

Live repro: registered a fresh tenant, went through the onboarding wizard to step 4 (NAV setup), entered deliberately invalid/junk NAV technical-user credentials, clicked "Kapcsolodas tesztelese". The real navPull() call fired against the actual NAV TEST API and correctly failed (502, funcCode=ERROR errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST) -- the wizard itself handled this honestly (error message shown, no fake success screen, confirmed the "Sikeres kapcsolodas" checkmark screen is correctly gated behind a non-demo response). Clicked "Kesobb" to finish onboarding and landed on the Statusz dashboard: the NAV kapcsolat tile shows green "Rendben" / "NAV bejelentkezesi adatok tarolva, automatikus szinkron aktiv." -- even though the ONLY sync attempt ever made for this tenant just errored out.

Why this matters for THIS persona specifically: the whole product pitch is reducing NAV-fear via a "the product watches for me" continuity loop (spec section 1.1). The Statusz dashboard tile is precisely the reassurance surface a NAV-fearing sole proprietor checks. Telling them sync is "active" when the credentials are actually broken is the exact kind of false reassurance that could lead to a real user believing their books are being kept automatically when they are not, only to find out at filing time.

Note: this is NOT the mk/ledger demo:true mechanism, which IS correctly gated (verified separately, honest "minta adat" warning shown). This is a second, independent status surface that does not check actual sync health.

Fix suggestion: track last-sync outcome (timestamp + success/failure) per tenant (e.g. alongside the credential row or a small sync-log table) and have this tile reflect it: ok only after a confirmed successful pull, warning/action_needed with the real error detail if the last attempt failed.

## d02bd609 — QQ voice dictation iOS message tells users to use Chrome, but Chrome-iOS has the exact same limitation (misleading dead-end advice)

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: low
- created: 2026-07-12 00:12 · last update: 2026-07-12 00:39

UAT (Scout) live sweep, card 6e2d04c5, follow-up on existing memory finding qq-voice-dictation-ios-disabled. apps/web/src/lib/dictation.ts unconditionally disables voice dictation on iOS via isIOS() BEFORE even checking for a SpeechRecognition constructor (any browser). The current disabledReason string shown to the user is: iOS: a hangfelismeres Safari-ban korlatozott -- hasznalj Chrome-ot. (iOS: speech recognition is limited in Safari -- use Chrome.) This is factually misleading: Apple requires ALL iOS browsers (including Chrome-iOS) to use the WKWebView/Safari engine, so Chrome on iOS has the identical Web Speech API limitation -- switching browsers will NOT fix anything, and the code itself disables dictation via the isIOS() check regardless of which browser constructor is present. A tradesman on an iPhone who trusts this hint will install Chrome, retry, and hit the same dead end. Severity: LOW (feature is a Could/nice-to-have per spec US-C1.2, not a blocker), but the copy actively suggests a non-existent fix, which is worse than a plain disabled state. Fix: change the copy to something accurate, e.g. A hangbevitel iOS-on egyelore nem tamogatott -- hasznald a szoveges/foto rogzitest. (drop the use Chrome suggestion).

## bf4570bc — HIGH: Zsibongo has no UI anywhere to invite staff login accounts (telephelyvezeto/gondozo/helyettes/eKepviselo) -- only reachable via raw API

- assignee: buildfejleszto · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-12 00:05 · last update: 2026-07-12 00:50

UAT (Scout), live sweep 2026-07-11/12 against suite-web-08wb.onrender.com / suite-api-08wb.onrender.com, fresh fenntarto tenant.

FINDING: the backend has a fully working POST /api/zsibongo/auth/invite {email,role,temporaryPassword,groupId?,childId?} route (fenntarto/telephelyvezeto-guarded) that creates a login-capable zsibongo_users row for any role (telephelyvezeto, gondozo, helyettes, eKepviselo, szulo). I used it directly via curl to provision 5 test personas and every login worked correctly.

BUT there is NO frontend control anywhere in the Zsibongo web app that calls this endpoint. Confirmed by:
- grep apps/web/src/api.ts for any zsibongo*Invite* function: zero matches (zsibongoLogin/zsibongoRegister exist, no invite wrapper).
- grep apps/web/src/views/Zsibongo*.tsx for invite/Meghivas/meghivo: zero matches (the only invite-flow code in the whole web app is for Eskuvo/LumaSeat, a different product).
- The Dolgozok (staff) tab is 100% read-only (ZsibongoView.tsx ~1856): a plain table, no add/invite button. The ONLY way to create a zsibongo_staff row is the one-shot Onboarding wizard step 3 (Vegyel fel dolgozokat, zsibongoCreateStaff) -- and that creates a STAFF PROFILE (name/role/group/shift/qualification) in zsibongo_staff, a completely separate table from zsibongo_users (login identity). Creating a staff profile does NOT grant login access.
- Live-confirmed: after registering a fresh tenant + creating a group + inviting 4 users via raw API (telephelyvezeto/gondozo/helyettes/eKepviselo), the Dolgozok tab and the Beosztas (shift schedule) tab both still show Nincs dolgozo felvette -- because the UI has no way to surface or create the corresponding staff/login link, and no way to invite at all.

IMPACT for the persona this product is built for (family-nursery owner opening a bolcsi, admin-dread): there is currently NO way, through the actual product, for a fenntarto to give their site manager, caregivers, or the state-reporting rep a login. The onboarding checklist 2/3 done screen (Vegyel fel dolgozokat) implies this is handled, but it only creates a non-login profile row. This is separate from the already-tracked, lower-priority parent-invite gap (card eb6510e8, waiting on guardian-persistence) and separate from the already-parked cross-tenant Helyettes-halozat marketplace (af31208d, deliberately on hold) -- this is the basic same-tenant staff/login invite, which appears to have simply been missed and is not tracked anywhere.

FIX SCOPE: add a Meghivas/invite control (likely on the Dolgozok tab, or as onboarding step 3b) that calls POST /api/zsibongo/auth/invite with role+email+temporaryPassword(+groupId for gondozo/helyettes), and ideally links the resulting user to the zsibongo_staff profile row (staffId param already supported server-side) so Dolgozok/Beosztas show a coherent picture. Architect/UX may want to weigh in on whether staff-profile-creation and login-invite should be merged into one flow.

Severity: high (core onboarding value prop for the primary persona is unreachable through the product), not blocker only because a temporary API-based workaround exists for support/CS to hand-provision on request.

## 31c675eb — QQ photo-estimate sends customer photos to direct (non-EU) Anthropic API, bypassing the DPA-approved bedrock-eu provider used by text structuring

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-12 00:11 · last update: 2026-07-12 00:58

UAT (Scout) live sweep, card 6e2d04c5, found while checking the two AI capture code paths separately per task instructions. Text structuring (POST /api/qq/structure) routes through apps/api/src/backends.ts selectLlm(), which on suite-api currently resolves to bedrock-eu (confirmed live via GET /health -> backends.llm:"bedrock-eu") -- this is the EU-hosted, DPA-covered provider that was explicitly approved for QQ AI-capture per agents/ba/deliverables/2026-06-20-kovetelmenyspec-quickquote-mvp.md ("AI-capture LLM-provider jovahagyva (EU-hosted Anthropic/Bedrock EU + DPA)"). However apps/api/src/qq-photo-estimate.ts:64 reads process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY directly and instantiates the raw @anthropic-ai/sdk Anthropic client -- this is the DIRECT (US/global, non-EU) Anthropic API, completely bypassing backends.ts and the bedrock-eu selector. Confirmed live: uploading a photo via the app successfully triggered a real Claude Vision analysis (POST /api/estimate/photo/quote returned real content), meaning ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set and this direct/non-EU path is actively serving customer photo uploads today. Photos are plausibly MORE sensitive than text notes (may contain faces, addresses, home interiors) and the architects own photo-estimate feasibility doc (2026-07-03) explicitly discusses EU-hosted inference + EXIF-strip + face-blur as GDPR requirements for this exact feature. Sending them to a non-EU API contradicts the products own approved data-residency posture. Severity: HIGH / compliance risk, not just UX -- recommend looping jogasz (Aegis) and architect (Atlas) in on remediation, not just a code fix. Fix: route qq-photo-estimate.ts through the same backends.ts multimodal-capable provider selection as text structuring (bedrock-eu supports Claude vision models too), removing the standalone ANTHROPIC_API_KEY direct client, or get an explicit DPA/legal sign-off if direct-Anthropic is intentionally kept for this one path.

## 0cc8587f — BLOCKER: Zsibongo landing trial-signup CTA permanently disabled (bolcsi-landing.onrender.com)

- assignee: frontendfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-12 00:04 · last update: 2026-07-12 01:04

UAT (Scout), live sweep 2026-07-11/12, https://bolcsi-landing.onrender.com/.

REPRO:
1. Open the live landing, scroll to #trial ("Probald ki 2 honapig ingyen").
2. Fill any/all fields, check the GDPR checkbox (#ctaGdpr).
3. The submit button (#ctaSubmit, "Ingyenes proba - 2 ho") NEVER enables, no matter what you do.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reading index.html + live Playwright test against the deployed URL, submitBefore/submitAfter both true=disabled):
- The form element has id=ctaForm, and JS calls handleSubmit(ctaForm, ...) at the bottom of the page.
- Inside handleSubmit, setupGdprToggle(formPrefix) is called with formPrefix=ctaForm, which then looks up qs(#ctaFormGdpr) and qs(#ctaFormSubmit) for the change-listener wiring.
- BUT the actual field ids in the HTML use prefix cta (not ctaForm): id=ctaGdpr, id=ctaSubmit, id=ctaEmail etc.
- qs(#ctaFormGdpr) and qs(#ctaFormSubmit) both resolve to null -> setupGdprToggle hits the early-return guard and NEVER attaches the change-listener that un-disables the submit button.
- Result: the button keeps its HTML disabled attribute forever. The entire trial-signup / waitlist form on the landing is unusable by any real visitor.

FIX (same pattern as the MikroKonyv landing, per landing-uat-sweep skill notes): make the form-id and the field-id prefix consistent. Simplest fix: rename the form element id from ctaForm to cta and call handleSubmit(cta, ctaSuccess, ...) instead of handleSubmit(ctaForm, ...). Verify against live deploy after fix: check GDPR box -> submit button must become enabled -> submit -> POST to suite-api-08wb.onrender.com/api/waitlist fires -> success screen shows.

SECONDARY (same page, bundle into this card): footer Feltetelek link points to /adatkezelesi-tajekoztato.html (privacy policy), but a separate real ToS page already exists and is live at /felhasznalasi-feltetelek.html (curl 200) -- it is just never linked. Point Feltetelek at /felhasznalasi-feltetelek.html instead.

Severity: blocker (primary conversion CTA on the whole product is dead). Repo: bolcsi-landing (standalone Render repo, not marveen-suite).

[Muse behavioral re-verify -- QQ R1 closeout] UX-1/2/4/5 re-verified. Method: live API round-trip against deployed suite-api-08wb.onrender.com (real registrations + login, since Chromium is broken in sandbox for a visual click-through) + code verify of f532730/fad5f22 + migration cross-check.

=== UX-1 (login profile rehydrate) -- PARTIAL PASS + 1 NEW RESIDUAL BUG ===
PASS (the HIGH part): registered a throwaway tenant, then LOGIN-ONLY (no register cache) -> response returns the REAL businessName + trades, NOT the "QuickQuote" placeholder. The client-facing leak (sendReply attributing client-portal replies to a placeholder name) is genuinely fixed. Reproduced clean on two separate accounts.

NEW BUG -- QQ-UX-1b (MED): taxNumber comes back NULL on login even though it was supplied at registration and IS persisted. Reproduced on two accounts (registered with 12345678-1-42 and 87654321-2-13, both login -> taxNumber:null). Root cause (confirmed, not assumed): register WRITES users.tax_number inside withTenant() (server.ts:1232-1244, sets app.tenant_id). The f532730 login lookup READS it with a BARE pool.query, no app.tenant_id (qq-auth.ts: SELECT (SELECT tax_number FROM users WHERE tenant_id=t.id) ...). users has RLS ENABLED (migration 0001 loop, tenant policy); migration 0084 set it NO FORCE -- but NO FORCE only exempts the table OWNER, and the app's non-owner/NOBYPASSRLS runtime role is STILL subject to the policy, so the subquery is filtered -> null. businessName/trades come from `tenants` (no tenant RLS policy) so they resolve. The commit's assumption "users is NO FORCE RLS -> safe for a bare pool.query" is the exact error -- 0084's own comment (line 15) describes this precise symptom. SAME bug class as the quotes-public-view RLS fix (server.ts:1268+). Fix: wrap the profile lookup in withTenant(pool, user.tenant_id, ...) or a transaction-local set_config('app.tenant_id',...), mirroring both the register write and the quotes-view fix. Impact: a VAT-registered vallalkozo logging in on a fresh device has null adoszam -> quotes/invoices generated in that session can omit a legally-mandatory field. Fresh-device-login + tax-field only, hence MED not HIGH.
(Known, correctly-disclosed gap, NOT a bug: phone/serviceArea also null -- no server-side column exists, pre-existing data-model gap Mason flagged honestly.)

=== UX-2 (logout) -- PASS (code + bundle) ===
QqView({reg,onLogout}); Kilepes button + confirm Modal (mirrors ZsibongoView); onLogout -> qqLogout()+state reset+setShowQqLogin(true) (login screen = account-switch); qqLogout() clears the qq_registration cache too. Logout is pure client-side so no API round-trip to assert; wiring is sound + mirrors the proven Zsibongo pattern. Residual: a visual click-through needs a browser (broken in sandbox) -- low risk given the mirrored pattern.

=== UX-4 (categories loading/error/retry) -- PASS (code) ===
categoriesLoading/categoriesError around a reusable loadCategories(); fieldset now shows loading msg OR error+retry button OR the categories; submit disabled w/ aria-describedby when categories never loaded. Mason confirmed qqTradeCategories() genuinely rejects on network failure (unreachable-port test) so the .catch() fires. Honest, actionable error copy.

=== UX-5 (register per-field a11y) -- PASS (code) ===
validate() -> per-field fieldErrors; aria-invalid + aria-describedby + role=alert per field (businessName/email/password/trades/terms); clearFieldError on change; top-level error retained for server errors. Exactly QqLoginView's proven pattern, now consistent across the product.

=== Net ===
UX-1 client-facing leak FIXED, UX-2/4/5 PASS. ONE new MED (UX-1b taxNumber RLS) opened by behavioral testing that diff-review could not have caught -- recommend a quick Mason follow-up (one withTenant wrap), then R1 fully closes. UX-3/6/7 still per earlier triage.

Visible result: broken-image icon instead of the photo the tradesperson just chose, right before they click Becsles keszitese -- looks broken/untrustworthy even though the underlying estimate call still works fine (upload goes via base64 in the POST body, unaffected by this CSP rule, confirmed the estimate itself completed normally). For a zero-patience persona this reads as "the app is broken," not "just a preview glitch." Checked sibling createObjectURL usages across MK/Eskuvo/Zsibongo -- all others are file-download `<a href>` links, not `<img src>`, so NOT affected by img-src; this is isolated to QQ's photo preview. Fix: add `blob:` to img-src in render.yaml's Content-Security-Policy header. Screenshot: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-iszzu-marveen-agents-uat/32695248-0e1d-4e4b-bc31-3fb583cc59f4/scratchpad/qq-uat/13-photo-selected.png.

## 1f8f02a5 — P0 SECURITY: Zsibongo self-fill routes unauthenticated cross-tenant data injection (children/staff/TAJ)

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-12 09:42 · last update: 2026-07-12 10:13

Verified P0 (deliverylead read the actual code at origin/main@2a6c6c7, not just the audit summary -- see fleet-security-incident-response skill requirement).

VULN: apps/api/src/zsibongo-routes.ts:2596 (POST /api/zsibongo/self-fill/parent) and :2641 (POST /api/zsibongo/self-fill/employee) are completely unauthenticated (no preHandler/guard at all), accept an arbitrary client-supplied body.tenantId, only check the tenant ROW EXISTS ("SELECT 1 FROM tenants WHERE id = $1"), then INSERT directly via bare pool.query (NOT wrapped in withZsibongoTenant) into zsibongo_children (with taj -- Hungarian social security number, Art.9-adjacent, feeds the real KENYSZI government report per this round's other finding) and zsibongo_staff. Comment above the code claims "the form link itself is the invitation" but there is NO token param in the body type and NO invite-token check anywhere in the handler -- any caller who has (or guesses/obtains) a valid tenantId can inject fabricated child/staff records into ANY Zsibongo tenant. Extra: the child INSERT hardcodes care_status='Felvett' (already-enrolled), contradicting the code's own comment that submissions should land "pending/unconfirmed for admin review" -- so an injected record doesn't even sit in a review queue, it looks live-enrolled immediately. Chained risk: this same unauth path can inject an attacker-controlled name string that later round-trips into the un-sanitized CSV exports (staff-supplements export routes ~2568/2577 + KENYSZI export ~969, no = + - @ neutralization) -- classic CSV/formula-injection vector if an admin opens the export in Excel.

STOPGAP (deploy now, P0, no design needed): disable both self-fill routes (503 "Ideiglenesen nem elerheto" or equivalent) until a real per-invite-token flow replaces the bare-tenantId design. This is the safe move per incident-response doctrine -- a rushed auth patch risks a worse silent bug; a clean disable has ~zero cost pre-launch (no confirmed real self-fill usage) and is instantly reversible.

STRUCTURAL FIX (round 2/3, needs real design, not a same-hour patch): admin generates a signed/random per-invite token (parent invite, employee invite) at creation time; self-fill routes derive tenantId server-side FROM the token record (never trust body.tenantId); wrap the insert in withZsibongoTenant; land submissions in a real pending/unconfirmed state, not care_status='Felvett'; add CSV-injection neutralization (strip/prefix leading =+-@) on every CSV export route as a separate hardening pass (staff-supplements + KENYSZI exports both affected).

ALSO FLAGGED (qa, same sweep): chat_audit_log has FORCE RLS with 0 policies (LOW/latent -- no write path exists yet, but if one gets added later it'll silently fail-closed-empty or need a policy add; track, not urgent).

GUARDRAIL: this class (route trusts body/caller-supplied tenantId with no server-derived identity) matches the fleet's known [[mvp-bearer-equals-tenantid-unauth-access]] pattern -- previous audit said Zsibongo/DORA were safe; this route slipped through because it's a body-param variant, not a bearer-header variant, and it's PUBLIC by design (not even the weak-bearer pattern). Fleet-wide PER-ROUTE re-audit needed (architect dispatched separately, card TBD) -- not per-product, per past lesson.

STRUCTURAL FIX DESIGN (ready to build, supersedes my earlier looser spec):
1. New table zsibongo_selffill_invites(tenant_id, group_id nullable, kind parent|employee, token UNIQUE random 32-byte base64url, created_by, revoked_at, expires_at), standard tenant RLS.

4. Self-fill routes take token in body, look up the invite row, generic 404 on not-found/expired/revoked (dont leak which), rate-limited per-IP using the decorator-based pattern (NOT the fastify@5.8.5-broken config-opt-in style).

6. Fix care_status hardcoded to Felvett -> pending value (check nothing else assumes Felvett is the only legal value first, e.g. KENYSZI/normativa aggregates).

POST /api/zsibongo/auth/invite succeeds (201, staffLinked:true). ## 6fb20fd9 — [Zsibongo] Self-fill employee submission fails for 2 of 3 roles, masked as fake 409 duplicate

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-12 13:11 · last update: 2026-07-12 16:53

E2E persona-flow verify (Marveen/deliverylead request, epic 3c8dcfcc, pairs with ecd41ae4+7cfda1cf), commit 55a4454 live. Full real-token flow tested: fenntarto creates a real invite via POST /api/zsibongo/self-fill/invites (no UI button for this exists yet, called the endpoint directly -- separate minor note below), opened the real link https://suite-web-08wb.onrender.com/self-fill-employee.html#tok=... as an unauthenticated applicant.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via direct DB migration read + request/response pairing, not guessed): the self-fill employee forms role <select> options are Gondozo(value=gondozo)/Helyettes(value=helyettes)/Telephelyvezeto(value=telephelyvezeto) -- but zsibongo_staff has CHECK (role IN (kisgyermeknevelo,segito,helyettes)) (migration 0018). Only helyettes happens to overlap. Submitting role=gondozo or role=telephelyvezeto throws a Postgres CHECK-violation on the INSERT, whose message contains violates -- the routes broad catch (err.message.includes(violates)) misreports this as {error: A jelentkezes mar be lett kuldve vagy utkozik egy meglevo rekorddal.} (409), which is FALSE: no record was ever created (confirmed via GET /api/zsibongo/staff showing no such row) and the applicant sees a confusing already-submitted message on their FIRST attempt with no way to recover.

Verified live with request/response capture:
- role=gondozo -> 409 fake-duplicate (2 of 3 dropdown options -- Gondozo, Telephelyvezeto -- are both broken this way)
- role=helyettes -> 201 real success

Downstream of the working case (helyettes), the rest of the flow is CLEAN: fenntarto Jelentkezesek tab shows a live nav badge count, the submission lists name/contact/role/group/date correctly, Elfogad approves it with a real state change (work_status jelentkezett -> dolgozik, is_active true, contact_email/contact_phone populated) and the tab correctly returns to empty after.

Not verified (out of scope for this pass, flagging as a related risk to check): the parent self-fill route uses the same broad violates-catch pattern, but its own INSERT uses a hardcoded server-side care_status=Jelentkezett literal (matches migration 0090s updated CHECK), so it is less likely to hit the same class of bug -- worth a quick confirm pass separately, not re-tested live here.

Minor separate note: no admin UI exists yet to CREATE a self-fill invite link (only the review/approve side from 7cfda1cf has a UI) -- I called POST /api/zsibongo/self-fill/invites directly via fetch with a real fenntarto session to get a real token for this test. Not a bug, just a gap if Istvan wants fenntartok to self-serve invite links without dev/API help.

Suggest fix: either (a) restrict the self-fill role dropdown to the same 3 values zsibongo_staff.role actually allows (drop Gondozo/Telephelyvezeto or map them to kisgyermeknevelo/telephelyvezeto-equivalent -- note telephelyvezeto is not a valid STAFF role at all per the CHECK, that may need a product decision on whether site-managers can even apply via this form), and (b) stop masking all violates errors as duplicate-submission -- return the real Postgres error class/code so a genuine constraint bug like this one fails loud in logs instead of silently misleading every affected applicant.

## 5d09fd5c — INFRA: root CLAUDE.md ancestor-inheritance leaks the restricted Render-key path to every agent

- assignee: devops · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-12 17:09 · last update: 2026-07-12 17:22

Found 2026-07-12 during epic 3c8dcfcc round 3 (a false security-alarm investigation, resolved as not-an-attack, but this real gap surfaced along the way).

The root /home/iszzu/marveen/CLAUDE.md contains a restricted section (agents/devops/.env.render path + source command for RENDER_API_KEY), whose own text says it is meant to be known only to marveen/deliverylead/devops, with build-agent CLAUDE.md files deliberately never referencing it.

BUT: CLAUDE.md files load by ANCESTOR DIRECTORY. Any agent whose cwd sits under the marveen root (e.g. agents/uat/, and presumably every other agents/<name>/ directory) automatically loads the ROOT CLAUDE.md as an ancestor context file, regardless of what that agents own CLAUDE.md says or omits. So the intended restriction is not actually enforced by any config -- it is a comment in a doc, contradicted by how the same doc gets loaded fleet-wide.

Confirmed concretely: a uat sub-session had full knowledge of the agents/devops/.env.render path (and had been running the source command itself, unprompted, for Render deploy-status checks all session) despite uats own CLAUDE.md never mentioning it.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) move the Render-key section out of the root CLAUDE.md into a file that is not ancestor-inherited by every agent (e.g. only loaded by marveen/deliverylead/devops explicitly), or (b) accept every agent under ~/marveen has effective read access to this path and adjust the trust model/restriction language accordingly (i.e. stop treating it as restricted if it cannot actually be restricted this way). Needs a decision on which, then implementation.

RETRACTING the not-an-attack framing this card was based on.
```json
{"label":"deadline_help","confidence":0.72,"reasoning":"The user asks about when to pay..."}
```
This looks like an internal routing/classification step (label/confidence/reasoning, clearly meant for backend logic) that is not being stripped from the model output before it is stored in the `message` field and sent to the client -- apps/api/src/ likely has a two-step prompt (classify then answer) where the classification response is being concatenated into the final message instead of consumed separately.

Severity varies by question:
- "Mikor kell befizetnem a kovetkezo adoeloleget..." -> JSON block, THEN a real helpful answer (deadline table) follows. Degraded but not broken.
- "szia" -> JSON block, THEN a real greeting response follows. Degraded but not broken.
- "Mi az a koltseghanyad, es hogyan valasszak?" -> the ENTIRE response IS JUST the JSON block. No actual answer is ever generated for this one -- functionally still broken for this question, just with a different symptom (raw JSON dump instead of a clean refusal).

Showing a first-time user a raw {"label":...,"confidence":0.82,...} blob is arguably MORE confusing/alarming than a clean refusal message -- it looks like a developer console leaked into the product. Please find where the classification-then-answer chain assembles the final message and strip the classification JSON before it reaches `message`/aiDisclosure, and separately investigate why the activity_classification-labeled path never produces a follow-up answer at all.

## dd6a40f5 — Zsibongo: Csoportnaplo shows literal "Invalid Date" (field-name mismatch, group-log endpoint)

- assignee: buildfejleszto · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-12 17:22 · last update: 2026-07-12 18:00

Found during UAT round 3 (card 65eeb5d8) gondozo (caregiver) persona daily-workflow pass on suite-web-08wb / suite-api-08wb.

BUG: on the gondozo Csoportnaplo tab, the auto-generated "Jelenlet" log entry (created when attendance is marked) shows the literal text "Invalid Date" where the timestamp should render. Reproduced live on a fresh synthetic tenant right after marking one attendance record.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via code read):
- GET /api/zsibongo/group-log in apps/api/src/zsibongo-routes.ts (~line 1335-1350) does `SELECT e.*, c.name AS child_name FROM zsibongo_daily_events e ...` -- the raw zsibongo_daily_events columns are `recorded_at`, `note`, `recorded_by` (see apps/api/db/migrations/0018_zsibongo_core.sql:272-282), NOT `created_at`, `description`, `created_by_name`.
- Frontend apps/web/src/views/ZsibongoView.tsx (~line 3535-3543) + the ZsibongoGroupLogEntry type (apps/web/src/api.ts ~2206-2212) expect fields named `created_at`, `description`, `created_by_name`.
- Since the API never returns those field names, `entry.created_at` is undefined on every row -> `new Date(undefined).toLocaleString("hu-HU")` renders as "Invalid Date" for EVERY Csoportnaplo entry (manual or attendance-derived), not just this one -- the fresh-tenant/first-attendance scenario is just the first time a row exists to expose it. `description` and `created_by_name` also silently render blank for the same reason (less visible than the date but same root bug).

FIX (backend-only, alias the columns to match the existing frontend contract -- the ZsibongoGroupLogEntry TS type already documents the intended shape):
```sql
SELECT e.id, e.event_type, e.note AS description, e.recorded_at AS created_at,
       COALESCE(s.name, e.recorded_by) AS created_by_name, c.name AS child_name
FROM zsibongo_daily_events e
LEFT JOIN zsibongo_children c ON c.id = e.child_id
LEFT JOIN zsibongo_staff s ON s.id = e.recorded_by
WHERE e.tenant_id = $1 ${date ? "AND e.time = $2" : ""}
ORDER BY e.recorded_at DESC
```
(Verify/adjust how recorded_by maps to a display name -- it may be a staff id, user id, or free text depending on caller.)

IMPACT: a raw JS error string ("Invalid Date") is visible to caregivers on a screen they use daily -- looks broken/unpolished and erodes trust, even though the underlying data is fine. Related to card e2fc35b2 (same general theme: SELECT * missing a needed JOIN/alias) but a different endpoint/table -- separate fix.

Please fix, deploy, and I will live-verify on suite-web-08wb before closing.

## 2858ad30 — Zsibongo: szulo (parent) can WRITE allergy data but cannot READ it back -- false "no allergy on file" risk

- assignee: buildfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-12 17:26 · last update: 2026-07-12 18:00

Found during UAT round 3 (card 65eeb5d8) szulo (parent) persona portal pass on suite-web-08wb / suite-api-08wb.

BUG: on the szulo Allergia tab, the page loads with a red error banner at the very top: "Nincs jogosultsagod ehhez a muvelethez." (You do not have permission for this action) -- yet the tab below it still renders normally with an empty state ("Nincs rogzitett allergia.") and a working "+ Allergia rogzitese" (add allergy) button.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via code read, apps/api/src/zsibongo-routes.ts):
- Line 664: `const ALLERGY_READ_ROLES = ["fenntarto", "telephelyvezeto", "gondozo", "helyettes"] as const;` -- szulo is NOT included.
- Line 720: `GET /api/zsibongo/children/:id/allergy` is guarded with `guard([...ALLERGY_READ_ROLES])` -- so a szulo caller is rejected with 403 before the handler body (and its assertChildInCallerGroup ownership check) even runs. Confirmed live: curl with a real szulo JWT against this route returns 403 "Nincs jogosultsagod ehhez a muvelethez."
- Line 769: `PUT /api/zsibongo/children/:id/allergy` is guarded with `guard(["szulo", "fenntarto", "telephelyvezeto"])` -- szulo IS explicitly allowed to WRITE.
- So a parent can submit/overwrite their childs allergy record via the PUT route (and the frontend explicitly offers them a "+ Allergia rogzitese" button to do so), but can never read it back via GET -- the read is silently rejected and the frontend falls back to an empty/"no allergy recorded" display.

SAFETY IMPACT (why this is more than cosmetic): if a childs allergy WAS already recorded (by staff or by the parent themselves on a previous visit), the szulo view will falsely show "Nincs rogzitett allergia." (no allergy on file) because the GET 403s and the UI treats that as empty rather than surfacing the permission error state. A parent checking whether their childs allergy is correctly on file would be given false reassurance. Staff/gondozo/fenntarto are unaffected (they ARE in ALLERGY_READ_ROLES) so the underlying data and caregiver safety workflow is fine -- this is specifically the parent self-service view being wrong.

FIX (minimal, backend-only): add "szulo" to ALLERGY_READ_ROLES (line 664) so GET /api/zsibongo/children/:id/allergy matches the PUT routes role list. The route already calls assertChildInCallerGroup() which has an explicit szulo branch (checks app.current_child, i.e. only the callers own linked child) -- so ownership scoping for szulo is already implemented and tested for this exact function, just never reached because the route-level guard() rejects szulo first. Also check GET /api/zsibongo/allergy-alert (line 818, same ALLERGY_READ_ROLES list) for the same gap if szulo is expected to see allergy-alert banners.

Please fix, deploy, and I will live-verify on suite-web-08wb before closing (both the 403 banner disappearing and that a real recorded allergy correctly displays for the parent).
