## e2fc35b2 — Zsibongo: Dolgozok list CSOPORT column always shows "-" (missing group JOIN)

- assignee: buildfejleszto · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-12 17:20 · last update: 2026-07-12 18:01

Found during UAT round 3 (card 65eeb5d8) operator persona onboarding pass on suite-web-08wb / suite-api-08wb.

BUG: on the fenntarto Dolgozok (staff) tab, the CSOPORT column always renders "-" for every staff member, even when the staff member IS correctly assigned to a group. Confirmed this is NOT a data problem: GET /api/zsibongo/staff returns group_id correctly set to a real group UUID, and the coverage math on Attekinto (workingStaff count, Lefedettseg=Megfelelo) correctly uses that assignment. So the assignment is saved and functionally used -- only the Dolgozok list display is broken.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via code read):
- Backend GET /api/zsibongo/staff in apps/api/src/zsibongo-routes.ts (~line 1158-1169) does a bare `SELECT * FROM zsibongo_staff WHERE tenant_id = $1 ORDER BY name` -- no JOIN to zsibongo_groups, so the response has no group_name field at all (undefined, not null).
- Frontend apps/web/src/views/ZsibongoView.tsx (~line 2142) renders `{s.group_name ?? "-"}` -- since group_name is always undefined from this endpoint, it always falls back to "-" regardless of group_id.
- Sibling endpoints already do this correctly, e.g. GET /api/zsibongo/my-children (~line 1871-1897) and GET /api/zsibongo/self-fill/pending (~line 2919-2927) both do `LEFT JOIN zsibongo_groups g ON g.id = s.group_id ... g.name AS group_name`. GET /api/zsibongo/staff was apparently never updated to match.

FIX (minimal, backend-only, no frontend change needed):
In apps/api/src/zsibongo-routes.ts GET /api/zsibongo/staff handler, change the query to:
```sql
SELECT s.*, g.name AS group_name
FROM zsibongo_staff s
LEFT JOIN zsibongo_groups g ON g.id = s.group_id AND g.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
WHERE s.tenant_id = $1
ORDER BY s.name
```

IMPACT: a fenntarto scanning the Dolgozok list to verify who is assigned to which group sees all dashes and would reasonably (but wrongly) conclude nobody is assigned -- undermines trust in the product for a core daily-admin screen, even though the underlying data/logic is fine.

Please fix, deploy, and I will live-verify on suite-web-08wb before closing.

## eb9496e5 — [Zsibongo] Csoportnaplo + Esemeny rogzitese completely broken -- frontend never sends groupId, every submit 403s via RLS

- assignee: fullstackfejleszto · priority: urgent
- created: 2026-07-12 18:00 · last update: 2026-07-12 18:12

Found while re-verifying dd6a40f5 live (card 65eeb5d8 / epic 3c8dcfcc round 3). The Csoportnaplo tab is ONLY reachable by gondozo/helyettes/fenntarto/telephelyvezeto (CAREGIVER_ROLES) -- in practice fenntarto/telephelyvezeto do not even have this nav tab, so gondozo/helyettes are the only real users of this feature.

BUG: clicking + Esemeny rogzitese opens a modal with just a Tipus <select> and a Leiras <textarea> -- no groupId field anywhere, visible or hidden. Selecting a type + filling the description + clicking Rogzites always returns:
```
403 POST /api/zsibongo/events {"error":"Nincs jogosultsag a muvelethez."}
```
This message is misleading -- it looks like a role-permission error but is NOT (confirmed: this exact string is the generic Postgres error-code map for 42501/insufficient_privilege in apps/api/src/shared/error-handler.ts, not the zsibongoGuard role-check message which reads differently: "Nincs jogosultsagod ehhez a muvelethez." with a possessive suffix). 

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via code read): the route handler (zsibongo-routes.ts ~1336, POST /api/zsibongo/events) does `body.groupId ?? null` -- since the frontend modal never sends groupId, every insert attempt by a gondozo/helyettes has group_id=NULL. The RESTRICTIVE RLS policy zsibongo_daily_events_group (migration 0037) requires `current_setting(app.current_role) NOT IN (gondozo,helyettes) OR group_id::text = current_setting(app.current_group)` -- with group_id NULL, `NULL::text = ...` evaluates to NULL (not TRUE), so the policy rejects the INSERT for every gondozo/helyettes caregiver, unconditionally.

VERIFIED live: same account, same request, but supplying groupId explicitly (read from the caregivers own JWT, which already carries group_id) -> 201 success, and the event appears correctly in Csoportnaplo (confirmed real date/description/created_by_name via dd6a40f5s just-verified fix).

IMPACT: the ENTIRE add-event feature on Csoportnaplo is unusable via the real UI, for every real caregiver, right now, on prod -- this is a daily-use feature (recording group activities), not an edge case. Given the caregivers JWT already carries their own group_id (per 62da86b8s fix earlier this round), the fix is likely a one-liner: have the frontend submit send `groupId: session.group_id` (or have the backend default `body.groupId ?? user.group_id ?? null` server-side as a safety net) instead of omitting it entirely.

Same likely applies to the sibling + Incidens rogzitese button -- not tested yet, worth checking the same modal/submit pattern.

**architect** · 2026-07-12 11:37

SPEC for 7cfda1cf: self-fill admin review/promote UI. Coordinated against Mason's ecd41ae4 (invite-token rebuild) -- one open item flagged below needs his 1-line confirmation, everything else is checked against real existing code (retention triggers, current staff shape), not guessed.

=== Data model (what "pending" means) ===
- Employee (unchanged, exists today): work_status='jelentkezett' AND is_active=false. No migration needed, this is already what self-fill/employee writes.
- Child (new, part of ecd41ae4): proposing care_status='Jelentkezett' as a new value added to zsibongo_children's CHECK constraint (currently only Jár/Beszokó/Felvett/Kifut/Szüneteltetett -- there is NO pending value today, Mason's migration has to add one). Naming mirrors staff's 'jelentkezett' for consistency. NEEDS MASON'S CONFIRMATION -- pinging him directly since he owns the migration and may have already picked something else.

=== IMPORTANT asymmetry Mason/Pixel should know about (found while checking existing retention triggers, migration 0054) ===
Staff: the INSERT-time retention trigger (zsibongo_staff_retention_clock_insert_trg) already starts a 3-year retention clock the moment is_active=false is inserted -- which is every pending applicant, from submission. So REJECT for staff needs no extra retention code, it's already ticking. APPROVE (is_active: false->true) automatically clears the clock via the existing UPDATE trigger -- also no new code needed, just a plain UPDATE.
Children: the retention clock is keyed specifically on care_status='Kifut' (or lifecycle='CLOSING'), NOT on any pending value at insert. So a pending child does NOT start any clock automatically -- REJECT for a child must explicitly set care_status='Kifut' to hook into the existing 5-year retention machinery, or it'll sit forever with no cleanup path. Not symmetric with staff, don't assume it is.

=== API contract ===
All new, admin-only (guard: fenntarto, telephelyvezeto), wrapped in withZsibongoTenant like every other admin write here.

GET /api/zsibongo/self-fill/pending
  -> { employees: [{id,name,email,phone,role,qualificationLevel,groupId,groupName,createdAt}], children: [{id,name,born,groupId,groupName,guardianName,guardianEmail,guardianPhone,createdAt}] }
  Sort oldest-first (createdAt asc) so nothing silently ages out unreviewed. Optional ?groupId= filter for multi-group tenants.
  Note: today email/phone/guardian-contact are stored stringly-encoded inside the `notes`/`grade` column (see the pre-fix self-fill INSERT code) -- if Mason hasn't already split these into real columns while rebuilding the insert path, this list endpoint needs to parse that structured string back out, or (better) Mason adds real columns now while he's touching this table anyway rather than parsing strings on every list call.

POST /api/zsibongo/self-fill/employee/:id/approve  body: {role, shift?, groupId?}
  -> UPDATE zsibongo_staff SET work_status='dolgozik', is_active=true, role=$role, shift=$shift, group_id=$groupId WHERE id=$id (tenant-scoped). Admin confirms/overrides role+group at approval time, not the applicant's self-reported hint. Retention clock auto-clears via the existing trigger, no new code.

POST /api/zsibongo/self-fill/employee/:id/reject  body: {reason?}
  -> UPDATE zsibongo_staff SET work_status='elutasitva' WHERE id=$id. is_active stays false (already was). No hard delete -- retention clock is already running since insert, existing nightly purge job handles eventual cleanup, no new logic needed.

POST /api/zsibongo/self-fill/child/:id/approve  body: {groupId?}
  -> UPDATE zsibongo_children SET care_status='Felvett', group_id=$groupId WHERE id=$id. This is exactly the state the old (buggy) code set immediately and for free -- now correctly gated behind admin action.

POST /api/zsibongo/self-fill/child/:id/reject  body: {reason?}
  -> UPDATE zsibongo_children SET care_status='Kifut' WHERE id=$id. Required (see asymmetry note above) to actually start the 5-year retention clock -- don't just leave it at the pending value.

=== UI placement ===
Checked: the existing "Dolgozok" (staff) admin tab is a flat read-only table, zero row actions today, and there's a separate existing children list/tab for caregivers already. Recommend NOT folding into either -- mixing pending intake into "who's currently working/enrolled" muddies both.

Found during R3 UAT UX pass (card 65eeb5d8, comment 4749). Kérlek fogalmazd át a kérdésedet.") each time. This message wrongly implies a user phrasing problem -- the failure is content-independent (fails even on totally benign input), so this looks like the underlying LLM call or the postguard check itself is erroring/misconfigured (fail-closed default), not legitimate per-question compliance moderation. Needs investigation of the mk-chat route + postguard logic (search apps/api/src for chat route + postguard/templateId) and the actual LLM backend call it makes -- check for an auth/config/timeout error being swallowed and converted into a generic refused response. ### Comments (7)

**fullstackfejleszto** · 2026-07-12 17:31

Root cause found + fixed, not a swallowed error -- the LLM provider (Bedrock-EU) throws cleanly on any real failure, which would surface as status:error not the observed postguard/422. Actual cause: has-ai-disclosure was a HARD output guard requiring the raw completion to independently self-disclose (literal marker/regex match), but the prompt only vaguely asked the model to include a disclosure with no literal text to copy -- so it almost never matched, refusing every response regardless of content. The real EU AI Act disclosure was never actually at risk: aiDisclosure=MI_DISCLOSURE is attached unconditionally on every success, thats the real delivery mechanism, the raw-text check was redundant. Downgraded that guard to soft, removed a second duplicate hard-substring check, and improved the prompt to literally ask for the marker (best-effort, not the compliance mechanism). Verified directly against the built gateway pipeline: a benign no-marker completion (reproducing the exact prod symptom) now returns status=ok with aiDisclosure correctly attached; a genuine tax-advice-language violation is still correctly blocked as postguard -- real guardrails untouched. Fix needed: either (a) GET /api/zsibongo/organization should merge tenant rule-pack-overrides on top of the institution-type defaults before returning rule_pack, or (b) the frontend Szervezet form should fetch+display from a real overrides-read endpoint. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed empirically, not just code-read): this was NOT the field-alias/key-mismatch class the R4 sweep had been finding all night -- it's the OTHER recurring class from earlier tonight (935a663a): raw-pool-query-rls-guc-bleed. zsibongo_rule_pack_overrides DOES have FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (confirmed live via pg_class/pg_policy -- relforcerowsecurity=true, policy tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')), applied via migration 0018's generic DO-loop over a table list rather than a literal per-table CREATE POLICY, which is why a plain grep for the table name never surfaced it. loadTenantRulePack() -- called by DOZENS of routes across the whole Zsibongo API, not just GET /organization -- read this table via a bare pool.query() with no app.tenant_id GUC set, so the LEFT JOIN's override columns always came back NULL regardless of whether a real override existed.

PROVED THE MECHANISM directly, not just inferred: ran the identical SQL as the qa superuser (returned the real override value correctly) vs as suite_app_runtime (the actual runtime role, returned NULL) -- confirmed the RLS filtering live, then confirmed loadRulePack() itself was already 100% correct in isolation (a manually-constructed override object applied fine). The bug was purely in how loadTenantRulePack fetched the row.

FIX: wrapped the read in withTenant() (only needs tenantId, not a full user object -- this function runs before some routes even resolve one).

VERIFIED end-to-end against a real local server + Postgres, before AND after the fix, same exact repro as your report: POST override default_fee_huf=12345 -> GET organization still showed 0 (bug reproduced) -> applied fix, fresh server process -> GET organization now correctly shows 12345. Since loadTenantRulePack feeds every route that needs capacity/normativa/fee numbers (not just organization), this fix has broader correctness impact than just the Szervezet tab display.

## d0a39a81 — [Zsibongo] Mai nap allergy-alert banner renders blank -- ": () —" instead of child name/allergen/severity

- assignee: - · priority: high
- created: 2026-07-12 18:31 · last update: 2026-07-12 18:51

Live-verified on suite-web-08wb.onrender.com, gondozo login (Kovacs Bela, tenant uat-r1-zsibongo-1783841275), Mai nap tab.

The caregiver landing page shows a safety banner "⚠ Allergia figyelmeztetes (1)" for the group, correctly counting 1 child with an allergy flag (child "UAT teszt adat" has allergy_alert:true per GET /api/zsibongo/today). But the detail line under the banner renders as literally:

: () —

-- no child name, no allergen, no severity, nothing actionable. Screenshot: cg_tab_Mai_nap.png.

Root cause traced via API: GET /api/zsibongo/today only returns a boolean allergy_alert per child -- no allergen name, severity, or note field at all. The frontend banner template (something like `${name}: ${allergen} (${severity}) — ${note}`) is being fed entirely undefined values, so it renders the templates bare punctuation with nothing filled in. This is the same class of frontend/backend field-contract gap flagged elsewhere this epic (groupId, Incidens group_id, Csoportnaplo description/note) -- here the backend response is simply missing the fields the frontend template expects.

Impact: this is a SAFETY-relevant broken warning shown on the caregivers primary daily-use screen (Mai nap) every day there is an allergy on file. A caregiver cannot tell WHICH child or WHAT allergen from this banner -- they would have to already know, or cross-reference the childrens table ALLERGIA column (which only shows a generic VAN/- badge, also no detail). Given persona Zsibongo = adminisztraciotol rettegő, gyerekkozpontu ember, a broken allergy-detail warning undermines core safety trust.

Fix: GET /api/zsibongo/today (and/or the children detail source) needs to actually return allergen name + severity + note per child so the frontend template has data to fill in; alternatively fix the frontend to gracefully hide the detail line (or fall back to just showing the childs name) when detail fields are absent, rather than rendering bare punctuation.

Fixed + deployed. marveen-suite commit a3da637, suite-api-08wb live.

So this route's raw-message leak was really only reachable via the JSON.parse path (now fixed with a clear message) -- the outer catch sanitization is a correct defensive backstop, not what was actually making that specific DB-error case safe.
